title: Veteran Spotlight: Bridget’s Path from the Navy to Array Labs
summary: Bridget, Capture and Proposal Manager at Array Labs, Navy Veteran
body_markdown:
Bridget is the only person in her family and friend groups who has ever served in the Navy. At 22, she drove to a strip mall where the military recruiting offices sat side by side and started shopping around. She was looking for a sense of purpose and maybe a little adventure. Her recruiter offered a slightly less glamorous perspective, warning that joining the Navy might be one of the hardest decisions she’d ever make, but that sticking with it would be worth it in the long run.


Bridget went on to serve 10 years in the Navy, building a career that took her through aviation, the legal field and eventually training and instruction. She started working with fixed-wing aircraft before transitioning to helicopters. Her job was to make sure every one of a helicopter’s thousands of parts was tracked, maintained, and reviewed before it left the ground. It was an environment where mistakes could have serious consequences, reinforcing a lesson she was taught throughout her career: “Complacency kills.” It was a blunt lesson, but one that taught her the importance of accountability and preparation, and of never getting so comfortable that you stop paying attention.


Bridget later transitioned into the Navy’s legal community as a paralegal. During a two-year assignment in Japan, she worked with local law enforcement on legal matters involving service members and helped sailors understand their responsibilities while stationed overseas. That work brought her closer to a career she had always been interested in pursuing.


Bridget is now attending law school, and she describes her time in the Navy as “a hugely big detour,” reflecting, “I think for me to get to law school, I had to kind of go through this crazy trajectory.”


When reflecting on her service, she says the Navy supplied the structure she was looking for. She earned her associate and bachelor’s degrees while serving, completed her master’s just three months after leaving the Navy, and credits the Navy with giving her the discipline to achieve her personal and academic goals.


The Navy also changed how she handles pressure. “When you operate in really dangerous environments and you come into environments where that is not as dangerous, I think you learn, this is not the end of the world. We’re going to be okay. We can figure this out.” She thinks veterans can bring a grounding presence to teams. “They can offer that calm to the storm.”


After leaving the Navy, Bridget continued supporting national security missions from the civilian side. Today she is a Contract and Proposal Manager at Array, supporting our work with government customers.


On Veterans Day, she thinks about what service costs. “You don’t go home for holidays. You’re not with your family. And some people make ultimate sacrifices.”


This Veterans Day, we’re grateful to Bridget and to everyone who gave up time, holidays and more to serve.
